description:
Missions - Renewed

WHAT DOES THIS MOD DO?
Once your colonies earn millions a month, a 30k bar mission is not worth the trip.
Missions - Renewed adds contracts in tiers 0 to 7, from pocket money to millions of credits.
Needs LunaLib.

Screenshots

Contracts in the bar

Every bar has a chance (50 percent by default) to have a mission board. "Open the mission board" lists 1 to 5 contracts by market size, each with its own tier and job type, for example "Tier 5 hauling": 1 or 2 at size 4 and 5, 2 or 3 at size 6, 3 or 4 at size 7, 4 or 5 at size 8, always 5 at size 9 and up. Size 3 markets rarely have a board, with 1 contract. Smaller markets have none.
Tiers are random, but lean a little toward your fleet size, colony income and credits. A late-game fleet sees fewer tier 0 jobs, and every tier stays possible.
Each contract pays an advance when you sign and the rest on completion.
Missing the deadline or abandoning the contract charges a penalty, even if that leaves you in debt, and costs reputation with the client's faction.
You can hold 3 contracts at once. They are in the intel screen under Missions.

Job types

Hauling: the client hands you the cargo: ore, metals, food, machinery and other trade goods. Deliver all of it to the named market before the deadline. Running off with the cargo costs more than it is worth.
Fuel run: the client fills your fuel tanks. Arrive with the full amount, so every jump on the way burns into the delivery unless you bring spare fuel.
Crew transport: contract workers ride in your crew quarters. Crew lost in battle count against the delivery.
Contribution: bring goods you find or buy yourself to a construction project. At tiers 4 to 6 the project may ask for a colony item instead.
Investment: put up a stake and get it back with profit after 5 to 12 months. No pulling out: the client calls the venture guaranteed, safe or risky, and a risky one can lose your whole stake. Pirates and the Luddic Path do not offer them.
Combat: someone was attacked near a planet in a nearby system and barely got away. Find the fleet that did it and destroy it. The offer shows a glimpse of the fleet.
Marine operation: raid a market hostile to the client to knock out a named industry, or bring your own marines to a garrison.
Expedition: haul supplies to a camp in an uncolonised system. Something may be waiting there; the terms say who is taking an interest in the route and how much.
Defense: a fleet is gathering outside a market of the client's faction and attacks when you arrive. Destroy it; the market's station fights with you. The offer shows a glimpse of the fleet.
Famous ship lead: pay for the location of one named, S-modded warship, from the tier's eighth of all warships by price: a pristine derelict to recover, or the flagship of a hostile fleet you can always recover once it is beaten.
Ship deal: a client wants one ship from your fleet and pays well over its value on the spot (more for a well-known ship with Starship Legends), or sells you a ship below its value, usually used with a few D-mods, rarely pristine. The offer shows the ship.
Conquest: capture a size 3 to 5 market of a faction hostile to the client. Tier 5 and up, needs Nexerelin. Story markets are never targets.
Salvage lead: pay for the location of a debris field, guarded by a few battered scavengers. The loot grows with the tier, up to colony items, AI cores and blueprints.
Docking at the destination completes a delivery job.
Clients you satisfy may offer to become contacts, more often at higher tiers.
Tier 0 hauling asks for 100 to 300 units and pays 1.5k to 6.5k. Tier 7 asks for 24,000 to 40,000 units and pays 1M to 1.3M. Hauling, fuel runs and crew transport pay a third of other jobs of the same tier, and combat pays less from tier 4 (1.2M to 1.6M at tier 7). Enemy fleets grow from about 10 DP at tier 0 to about 500 DP at tier 7.

Settings and compatibility

LunaLib settings: chance of a mission board per bar, Proving yourself (finish lower tiers to unlock higher ones, two tiers at a time), how much the tier roll leans toward your strength, lowest and highest tier, each job type on or off, reward multiplier, a pay multiplier for each job type, enemy strength multiplier.
Debug section in LunaLib with a test mode, off by default: spawn any job type at any tier at any bar, and complete or fail open contracts at once.
Does not take a place from other mods' bar events.
Can be added to a game in progress. Removing it from a game in progress breaks that save.

Text (readme and this post): Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)

Version log
0.8.8
Famous ships are held by pirates or the Luddic Path, or by any other faction you are not friendly with (reputation 10 or lower), Legio Infernalis included. This goes for a famous flagship's fleet and for the fleet guarding a famous derelict. Fighting them never costs reputation.

0.8.7
Fixed famous ship leads that said "That contract is no longer on offer" when clicked. A flagship's escort can now be any pirate, Pather or Legio fleet, whoever the client is at war with, and a lead looks further out when nothing is in range.
The mission board checks its contracts when it opens and leaves out any that cannot be offered, so the count and the list only show contracts you can open.

0.8.6
Famous ship leads cost more: 40% of the ship's value plus 5% per S-mod (was 15%).

0.8.5
Famous ship lead prices follow the ship's value again (15% of it, plus 5% per S-mod), with no cap by tier.
Famous ship derelicts vary: some are unguarded, some have scavengers nearby, some sit under a guard fleet of varying strength. Flagship escorts vary in strength too. The offer says which, and about how many DP.
Removed the 0.8.4 check for replaced star systems. Systems are only replaced while the sector is generated, before any contract exists, so it could never trigger.

0.8.4
Contracts may send you into dangerous systems again (Remnant strongholds, Blade Breaker bases and the like), and high tier famous derelicts usually lie in one.
A contract pointing into a star system that another mod removed and replaced is withdrawn from the board, or, if already signed, ends as void with the lead fee refunded. Before, the ship or debris field could sit in a system that no longer exists.

0.8.3
Contracts no longer send you into dangerous or story systems, such as Blade Breaker bases from Dassault-Mikoyan Engineering, Remnant strongholds, or systems a quest already uses. This covers famous ship leads, salvage leads, combat targets and expeditions.

0.8.2
Famous ship leads pick by price: all warships are sorted by value and split into 8 equal groups, tier 0 the cheapest and tier 7 the most expensive, and the ship is drawn at random from its tier's group. One very expensive modded ship no longer pushes every tier up.
Famous ships always have S-mods: 1 at tiers 0 to 2, 2 at tiers 3 to 5, 3 at tiers 6 and 7.
A famous ship lead never costs more than half of what a contract of its tier pays.
Proving yourself opens tiers two at a time: tiers 0 and 1 are open from the start, 3 contracts of tier 0 or higher open 2 and 3, 3 of tier 2 or higher open 4 and 5, and 3 of tier 4 or higher open 6 and 7. New LunaLib setting for how many tiers open at once.
With Tahlan Shipworks, the Legio Infernalis turns up wherever pirates do.

0.8.1
Tier 5 to 7 combat, defense and expedition enemies are now mostly elite war fleets of a faction at war with the client. Anything stranger is very rare.
Famous ship leads bring better warships at higher tiers: no freighters or transports, and no pirate or Luddic Path refits from tier 4.
Ship sales: most ships for sale are used, with 1 to 4 D-mods and a lower price. Pristine ships are rare.
Investment terms read "Risk: Safe" (or Guaranteed, Risky).
Expedition terms say who is taking an interest in the route and how much, for example "Pirate interest: Severe".

0.8.0
Offers show the ship on the right for ship deals and famous ship leads.
Combat and defense offers show a glimpse of the enemy fleet: its biggest ships and an estimate of its size in DP.
Ship deals: instead of ordering a hull for later, a client now asks for one ship from your fleet and pays well over its value on the spot. With Starship Legends, well-known ships fetch more.
Defense: the attacking fleet appears as soon as you sign and waits outside the market. It attacks when you arrive in the system.
Investments: no more pulling out early. Each venture is guaranteed, safe or risky, in the client's words. Safe ventures rarely fail and return half the stake; risky ones pay much more but can lose all of it.
Conquest: from tier 5 only. Tier 5 asks for a size 3 market, tier 6 size 4, tier 7 size 5. Story markets such as Chicomoztoc and Gilead are never targets.
Salvage leads: more colony items, AI cores, hull mods and blueprints at higher tiers, and a few battered scavenger ships guard the field.
Expeditions say how likely an ambush is in words (unlikely, possible, likely, almost certain) instead of a percentage.
Offers are written in the client's own voice.
New LunaLib setting "Proving yourself", on by default: clients offer work one tier above what you have done. Finish 3 contracts of a tier (or higher) to open the next one; the number is a setting too. Buying or selling ships and investments do not count.

0.7.1
Contracts per mission board now follow market size: 1 or 2 at size 4 and 5, 2 or 3 at size 6, 3 or 4 at size 7, 4 or 5 at size 8, always 5 at size 9 and up. Size 3 markets rarely have a board, with 1 contract. Smaller markets have none.

0.7.0
New mission board: one "Open the mission board" option at the bar lists 2 to 5 contracts, more at bigger markets, each with its own tier and job type. Signing one leaves the others on the board.
Ship hand-overs and the test mode spawner moved onto the board.

0.6.0
New job type: defense. A fleet will attack a market of the client's faction in a set number of days. Be there and destroy it.
New job type: famous ship leads. Pay for the location of one named ship sized by the tier: a pristine derelict to recover, or the flagship of a hostile fleet.
New job type: ship deals. A client pays well for a hull you bring to their bar, or sells you a pristine ship below its value.
New job type: conquest, tier 3 and up. Capture a market of a faction hostile to the client. Needs Nexerelin.
New job type: salvage leads. Pay for the location of a debris field with loot by tier.
LunaLib switches for the new job types, and pay settings for defense, ship orders, conquest and salvage lead loot.

0.5.0
New LunaLib section "Pay per job type": a pay multiplier for each job type, on top of the reward multiplier. It changes the money, not the cargo or marines asked for.

0.4.6
Combat pays less from tier 4 up: 75 percent of before at tier 4, 60 at tier 5, 50 at tier 6 and 40 at tier 7.
Smuggling is removed. A smuggling contract you already signed can still be finished.

0.4.5
Hauling, fuel runs and crew transport pay a third of what they did. The cargo they ask for is unchanged.

0.4.4
Update checkers and mod managers now link to the forum thread.

0.4.3
Fixed a crash when opening the intel screen with a combat contract.
Combat contracts no longer say who the enemy is. You only know where someone was attacked.
Enemy fleets are much smaller at low tiers and are now measured in deployment points: about 10 DP at tier 0, 45 at tier 2, 180 at tier 4 and 500 at tier 7.
Hauling asks for more cargo at higher tiers, up to 24,000 to 40,000 units at tier 7.
Offers name the client who supplies the cargo, and the penalty line now reads "Contract failed".
Shorter LunaLib descriptions.

0.4.2
New gold icon in mod managers (TriOS) and in LunaLib's settings.

0.4.1
Fixed: after your first contract in a session, the next bar offer closed the moment it opened.
Some enemy fleets are now built the way the game builds its own, with the matching loot.
Leftover contract fleets now leave. Offers that cannot be built no longer risk a crash.
New contacts have a contact type, so they offer work.

0.4.0
New job types: combat, marine raids and garrisons, expeditions, smuggling.
Clients you satisfy may offer to become contacts.
LunaLib: switches for the new job types and an enemy strength multiplier.

0.3.0
LunaLib: turn each job type on or off, and set the lowest and highest tier bars offer.
Test mode moved to its own Debug section in LunaLib.

0.2.0
New job types: fuel runs, crew transport, contributions (including colony items at tiers 4 to 6) and investments.
New LunaLib test mode: spawn any contract at any bar, and complete or fail open contracts at once.
Fixed: a bar with no contract on your last visit could hide its next contract for up to 40 days.

0.1.0
First release: tiered bar contracts and the first job type, hauling.

Job types include hauling, fuel runs, crew transport, combat, defense, expeditions, ship deals, and conquests. Contracts pay advances and penalties for failure, with options to unlock higher tiers by completing lower ones.
